text: In this step, you choose based on what matters most to you right now: either creating an invoice or offer and sending it to your client – or getting your crew started in the app first.
They can register their hours manually or clock in automatically with GPS. We'll start with that step.
First, we create our first project.
Choose Location and search for the project address.
Here you set the GPS radius – here we reduce it to 200 metres. It's the area where the work shift starts or ends automatically, if the employee has chosen to clock in that way.
By default, the project name comes from the address – and you can always change it.
Here we enter the order reference. These numbers follow the project all the way and end up on the invoice.
Next, we add an employee to the project team.
Enter their email address – the invitation is sent there.
You can choose which language the email is sent in and which language the app will be in, as well as the person's role.
Done – the invitation has been sent.
Here you set the start and end of the work shift. Based on these times, the planned hours are filled in automatically in the shift schedule.
The start and end dates are also shown in the planning view.
The budget figures appear in the budget card.
Done – the project is created.
Now let's move on and create a task.
We start with a description of the task itself.
Here we choose the project we just created.
By default, everyone on the project is notified – but you can limit the push notifications to specific team members.
Today's date is preset – of course, you can change it.
Here we set a deadline – for example, 14:00.
Until the person marks the task as done, a reminder is sent every 15 minutes – you can change that, of course.
And after a certain number of reminders – in this case three – the manager gets a message.
Save – the task is created.
Then we move on to adding tools.
An admin can assign a tool manually, as we do here – or a worker can scan the tool's QR code in the app to register it to themselves.
We can assign the tool to an employee or link it to a project.
You can also add a note.
Save – now you always know where the tool is and who is responsible for it.
Your crew is up and running! Next, let's go through every step of creating your first invoice.
